recovery.settingsIntro: Optional. Use it to recover this device's vault when the master password is forgotten. The recovery key is a 72-character hexadecimal string; the recovery kit is that key together with its kit id, downloadable as an .aphrecovery file. Anyone holding the recovery key and a copy of this vault can decrypt your data, so keep the kit offline — apart from this computer and from your backups. A recovery kit is not a backup: it only unlocks the current vault on this device, cannot bring back deleted data, and does not carry over to another machine.
recovery.enabled: Offline recovery is enabled on this device.
recovery.disabled: Offline recovery is not enabled on this device.
recovery.currentPasswordPlaceholder: Verify your current master password before replacing or disabling
recovery.replaceWarning: The current kit stays valid until you confirm the replacement. Cancelling does not change it. You only need your current master password, not the old recovery key. A replacement rotates this device's vault only — it cannot revoke a vault copy or kit file someone has already taken. Change your master password if you suspect a leak.
recovery.disableWarning: This only removes the local recovery entry. It cannot revoke material that has already been copied, including a vault copy or an older kit file someone took. If you suspect a leak, change your master password.
recovery.disableConfirm: I understand and want to remove this device's recovery entry.
recovery.disabledSuccess: Offline recovery disabled on this device.
recovery.activated: Recovery kit confirmed and activated. Store it securely offline.
recovery.saveWarning: Download the kit, or write the recovery key out in full, and keep it somewhere you can reach without unlocking this vault. The kit file is UNENCRYPTED plaintext — anyone who has it can decrypt this device's vault. Guard it like a password: don't leave it in Downloads, and don't send it by email or cloud drive. Nothing has been enabled or changed yet. The next step hides the original code, so confirm by entering it back from the copy you just saved.
recovery.plaintextAck: I understand the kit file is unencrypted plaintext: anyone who has it and this device's vault data can decrypt it. Guard it like a password.
recovery.savedContinue: I saved it — hide the key
recovery.reenterHint: The original key is now hidden. Enter the key from your saved copy, or select the file you downloaded. Do not rely on this window as your only copy.
recovery.confirmKey: Key from the saved new kit
recovery.uploadKit: Or select a local recovery kit file
recovery.fileTooLarge: The recovery kit exceeds the limit (16 KiB file / 4096 characters). Select a valid .aphrecovery file.
recovery.resetIntro: Use the offline recovery key created in advance for this device's current vault. Recovery re-encrypts the vault with a new master password and replaces the recovery kit. No data is sent anywhere.
recovery.keyFormatHint: It looks like 1a2b3c4d-… (72 hex characters in total). Spaces, hyphens and letter case are all accepted, and you can also paste the full contents of a .aphrecovery file.
recovery.newPasswordPlaceholder: At least 8 characters, with letters, numbers and symbols
recovery.passwordMismatch: The new passwords do not match.
recovery.passwordRequirements: Use at least 8 characters including letters, numbers and symbols; avoid common passwords. Leading and trailing spaces are ignored.
recovery.prepareReset: Verify key and prepare new kit
recovery.rekeyWarning: This password change also replaces the recovery kit. The old kit will no longer work with the current vault. Old backups still require the password used when they were exported. Save and confirm the new kit before continuing.
recovery.resetSuccess: Recovery complete. The vault remains locked. Close this dialog and unlock with your new master password; it will not be filled in automatically.
recovery.skipConfirm: I understand those records will stay permanently unreadable, and I still want to recover the rest.
recovery.skipNote: Some records on this device cannot be decrypted with this key, so the recovery was aborted to keep it atomic. If you continue, those records stay in the vault exactly as they are and remain permanently unreadable under the new master password, while everything else is recovered. You can also step out and try a different key or an encrypted backup first.
recovery.skipChangeConfirm: I understand those records will stay permanently unreadable, and I still want to change the master password.
recovery.skipChangeNote: Some records on this device cannot be decrypted with the current key, so the password change was aborted to keep it atomic. If you continue, those records stay in the vault exactly as they are and remain permanently unreadable under the new master password, while everything else is re-encrypted. You can also step out and try the old master password or an encrypted backup first.
recovery.resetPartialNote: This recovery skipped some records that could not be decrypted: they are still in the vault, but no longer readable.
recovery.partialChangeNote: The master password was changed, but {count} record(s) could not be decrypted and were carried over as-is; the new master password cannot read them. Review and handle each one yourself.
recovery.relockRequired: The master password was changed, but this session could not be refreshed. Close this window and unlock again with the new master password.
recovery.notEnabled: Offline recovery must be set up before you forget your master password. This device has no enabled recovery entry. A key cannot bypass this requirement or restore missing data.
recovery.corrupted: The recovery configuration is incomplete or damaged. Replace it using your current master password, or disable it. Existing data has not been cleared.
recovery.corruptedLocked: The local recovery configuration is incomplete or damaged. Recovery cannot continue. Existing data has not been cleared; keep your backup files safe.
recovery.error.invalid: The recovery key or kit is invalid or does not match this vault. Check your saved material and try again. No data was cleared.
recovery.error.stale: The vault or recovery settings changed. Go back and create a fresh kit before confirming.
recovery.error.replacementRequired: An active recovery entry requires a new recovery kit for this password change. Go back and prepare one.
recovery.error.incomplete: Some local data could not be decrypted with this key, so recovery was aborted and nothing changed. Try another recovery key or encrypted backup, and do not clear your data.
recovery.error.undecryptableRecords: Some records on this device cannot be decrypted with the current key, so the password change was aborted and nothing changed. You can only continue after explicitly accepting that those records stay unreadable.
recovery.error.samePassword: The new master password matches the current one, so the data key would not change and existing recovery material would stay valid. Please choose a genuinely different master password.
recovery.error.corrupted: The local vault data is incomplete or corrupted, so this key change was cancelled and nothing was written.
recovery.error.weakPassword: The new master password does not meet the requirements: at least 8 characters including a letter, a number, and a symbol.
recovery.error.wrongPassword: The current master password is incorrect.
recovery.error.emptyPassword: Enter a non-empty master password. Leading and trailing spaces are ignored.
recovery.error.concurrentWrite: Another window changed the vault. No password change was committed. Go back and try again.
recovery.error.busy: The vault is busy with another operation. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
recovery.error.failed: The operation could not be completed. Keep your current password and recovery material, and try again. No data was cleared.
